title: Compute 'the prompt is completely built' section by section from cited evidence, conjunctively, with the ask set pinned
problem: On 2026-10-30 the founder set the completion criterion: "That is done when we completely build the prompt" (INTENT-20261030-BUILD-BEFORE-DEVICE-RUN). The prompt is the 77-section directive of 2026-10-28. Nothing computed that sentence. The path's depth covers nodes N1-N8 only, so reaching N8 could be read as 'the prompt is built' while whole sections stayed open (the unit spec names sections 11, 26, 28, 32, 33, 36, 37, 42, 50 and 52). That is a false-completion risk, and directive sections 10 and 73 say 'Never fabricate completeness' and 'Never inflate completeness'.
founder_intent_refs: INTENT-20261030-BUILD-BEFORE-DEVICE-RUN (the criterion: "That is done when we completely build the prompt")
INTENT-20261028-OPUS-MAXIMUS-REISSUE (sections 10 and 73: never fabricate or inflate completeness; the map reads all 77 sections; sections 12, 68 and 69 hold the asks the merged #236 closed)
baseline: feb531d2 (#227's branch, recording the directive and the correction): the acceptance harness checks acceptance/missions.json and acceptance/completion-contract.json (Missions A-L and the section-35 functions). No file maps the 77 directive sections, and `python -m acceptance check` reads no directive map, so a map claiming all 77 sections DONE, with section 40 removed and section 13's heading changed, passes with exit 0 'sound' (vacuously: the base has no directive gate, review finding F8).

alternatives.name: Proposed: a pinned, conjunctive section map inside the existing acceptance harness
alternatives.description: acceptance/directive-sections.json holds one record per section 1-77 with the source's exact heading and its testable asks (paraphrase, verbatim excerpt, the listed lines it answers, owner paths, cited evidence, required tier, computed tier, coverage, blocker with its record). acceptance/directive.py computes each ask's tier as the least-verified of what it cites (as the harness does), counts an ask met only at its required tier and covered, a section DONE only when every ask is met and every listed line is answered or set aside, and 'completely built' only when no ask is BUILDABLE_NOT_BUILT, an unguarded principle or open with no blocker, and every listed line is accounted for. acceptance/directive-asks.pin.json pins every ask id; asks are retired, never deleted; `directive --against <base>` refuses a pin edited in the same change. A separate workflow collects every cited node and runs an 85-mutant gate.
advantages: The founder's sentence becomes one computed answer with reasons: on the merged tree 'prompt completely built: NO', 77 of 272 asks met at the static ceiling, 130 open asks building can still close
The buildable residual is printed in dependency order (68 rows on the merged tree), a work queue derived from the same map
Reuses the harness's report, node resolution and real-process rule; completion-contract.json and missions.json are cited as evidence, not copied
Deleting or relabelling an ask, citing a helper, claiming a tier above the evidence and calling an under-mapped section DONE are each refused by name (37 tests, 85 of 85 mutants caught)
disadvantages: The map is a reviewed reading of the directive; paraphrase fidelity, required tiers and blocker classes are judgements no check can make
Counts are static ceilings; CI collects the cited nodes but does not run them
Large: 6,004 lines of map and 714 lines of checker to keep current as units land

alternatives.name: Simplest viable: one record per section in completion-contract.json citing tests, tier computed, no pin and no line accounting
alternatives.description: The unit spec's literal wording ('extend the existing acceptance/completion-contract.json harness ... a section entry citing a non-existent test, or claiming a level above its evidence kind, fails'). Round 1 of this unit (4a4facc6..b909b516) was close to it: 258 asks, 19 tests, 29 mutants, no pin, no listed-line accounting.
advantages: Already refuses a non-existent test and a tier above the evidence
disadvantages: The round-1 attack review reproduced that deleting an open founder ask turned its section DONE with `check` and all 19 tests passing; deleting all 189 open asks flipped both verdicts to yes (MWB-1)
Section 69 computed DONE on one ask for twelve bullets and four prohibitions (MWB-2, F2), so round 1 reported DONE 3 where line accounting gives DONE 1
alternatives.revival_evidence: A founder ruling that the ask set is fixed by him and signed, which would make the in-repo pin unnecessary.

alternatives.name: Strongest competing design: completion computed from a CI run of every cited node, with a founder-signed ask set
alternatives.description: Run every node the map cites in CI with Chromium, bubblewrap and a DALEOBANKS checkout, publish `directive --outcomes`, and accept a change to the ask set only under a founder signature.
advantages: Attained tiers instead of static ceilings: the 6 asks met only statically (skips on every host checked) would show as unmet
A pin change could not pass without the founder
disadvantages: No workflow in the repository provisions Chromium, bubblewrap or a DALEOBANKS checkout today
A founder signature on every map edit adds founder burden for bookkeeping
alternatives.revival_evidence: The #196 integrator adds a CI job with Chromium and bubblewrap that runs the cited nodes; or the founder asks to sign the ask set.

alternatives.name: Staged and reversible: report only first, gates later
alternatives.description: Land `python -m acceptance directive` as a read-only report, and add the pin, the line accounting and the mutant gate only after the founder ratifies the reading.
advantages: Smallest first change; the reading can be corrected before anything gates on it
disadvantages: A report without the pin is the version the review showed could be edited into 'completely built: yes' with every check green
Gates that arrive later must be reviewed again against a map that has moved
alternatives.revival_evidence: The founder rejects the reading wholesale, so the gates would only protect a wrong map.

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: The founder's criterion stays uncomputed. Completion is judged from path depth or prose reports, and the false-completion risk the unit spec names remains.
advantages: No new map to maintain as units land
No new workflow or 30-minute mutant gate
disadvantages: No answer to 'is the prompt completely built' that a test can check
No ordered list of what building can still close
Sections 10 and 73 ('Never fabricate completeness', 'Never inflate completeness') stay unguarded for completion claims

roles.position: The founder's own sentence is the criterion, and it is now computed conjunctively: every section, every ask, every listed line. It answers NO on the merged tree, which is the truthful answer. Nothing is retired without a founder intent record quoted verbatim, so no ask leaves by an agent's choice.
material_concerns: The 4,026-character preamble before section 1, including the 'Build this:' paragraph, is not mapped, and the README and the summary line do not say so (review MWB-11, not addressed)
Required tiers and blocker classes are this session's reading; the founder has not ratified them
655 listed lines in 55 sections have no ask yet, so the per-section counts may hide asks

roles.position: One harness, not a parallel framework: directive.py reuses acceptance/__init__.py's report, node resolution and real-process rule, and asks cite completion-contract.json functions and missions.json requirements as evidence. The map is a new data file beside them rather than records inside completion-contract.json, because the directive's 77 sections are a different key space from the section-35 functions; this departs from the spec's wording and is recorded.
material_concerns: Every landing unit changes what evidence points at; the map must be re-read after each integration (shown when #236 and #234 needed c49572d7)
The map is 6,004 lines; one file edited by many units will conflict if several edit it at once
The pin is in-tree; only `--against` a base refuses a pin edited together with the map

roles.position: Two reviews of round 1 (b909b516) were done by separate agents of this same session, one attack and one fidelity, not by independent sessions or humans. They reported 20 findings. The 18 the fix round took up were reproduced and fixed, each with a regression test, and the mutant gate grew from 29 to 85. Two were not changed: the unmapped preamble (MWB-11) and the vacuous base fail-before (F8, a wording point). A final verification by another agent of this session re-ran the gate (85 of 85) and corrected one README count.

A blocker record shows a blocker exists, not that nothing else blocks; relabelling within the pinned class is still a review question

The cost is maintenance: each unit that lands must cite its tests in the map (the check refuses a stale tier), and the integrator re-reads the map after each merge.

pass_1.intended_outcome: Any claim that the prompt is completely built is computed from the directive's own sections and the tests that exist, refused while any part is open, and cannot be produced by editing the map.

advantages.statement: One conjunctive answer to the founder's criterion
advantages.amplified_value: Completion claims in reports and PRs can be checked against `python -m acceptance check` instead of prose; a later report saying 'built' while the check says NO is visibly wrong

advantages.statement: The buildable residual in dependency order
advantages.amplified_value: The same map that refuses false completion orders the remaining work; when a unit lands, the asks it closes move and its row leaves (WU-01 and WU-14 did, 70 rows to 68)

advantages.statement: Reuse of the acceptance harness's rules and evidence
advantages.amplified_value: An ask's tier is computed exactly as a mission requirement's or contract function's is, so the two cannot disagree on what a test can establish

disadvantages.statement: The ask set is a human reading; deleting or relabelling an ask could fake completion
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Pin every ask id with the class it may claim; retire, never delete; FOUNDER_ONLY and EXTERNAL on test-reachable tiers cite a record; `directive --against <base>` ratchets in CI on pull requests

disadvantages.statement: Statuses are static ceilings and can be read as attained
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Every count is labelled 'static ceiling' or 'in this run'; `directive --outcomes` recomputes from a run, where a failure, skip or empty collection leaves the ask unmet; the LOCAL runs are committed per ask

disadvantages.statement: A section with too few asks computes DONE
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Listed-line accounting: every bullet and every 'Do not' or 'Never' line must be answered by an ask or set aside with a reason before DONE or 'completely built'

disadvantages.statement: CI cost and fragility: cited files need networkx, scipy and Playwright to collect, and the mutant gate takes about 30 minutes
disadvantages.redesigned_response: A separate workflow installs dev, cognition and playwright==1.63.0 with a read-only token; canonical-ci.yml is not edited, so the integrator decides where the gates run

disadvantages.statement: Every landing unit must update the map
disadvantages.redesigned_response: The check refuses a stale tier or a closed unit still named by an open ask, so an outdated map fails instead of drifting; the integrator re-reads it after each merge, as c49572d7 did

comparisons.baseline: feb531d2: no directive gate; any content in a directive map passes
comparisons.do_nothing: The criterion stays uncomputed and completion is judged from path depth or prose
comparisons.simplest_viable_alternative: Round 1 without pin or line accounting: reproduced bypasses to 'completely built: yes' and DONE 3 on under-mapped sections
comparisons.strongest_competing_architecture: CI-run outcomes plus a founder-signed ask set: attained tiers, but needs CI provisioning that does not exist and founder signatures on bookkeeping
comparisons.reversible_experiment: This change: data files, a checker and a separate workflow; no runtime reads them; one revert restores the earlier check

rejected_alternatives.name: Records inside acceptance/completion-contract.json
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Its records are the section-35 functions with their own schema; mixing 77 section records into it would change that contract's schema and fields; the map cites its functions instead
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: The completion-contract owner asks for one file

rejected_alternatives.name: Map only the sections the spec named (11, 26, 28, 32, 33, 36, 37, 42, 50, 52)
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: The criterion is the whole prompt; a partial map would recreate the false-completion risk for the other sections

This pass attacks the strengthened design for gaming, unrun evidence, scope, drift after merges and maintenance.

pass_2.final_design: acceptance/directive-sections.json (77 sections, 272 pinned asks, 69 units) checked by acceptance/directive.py through `python -m acceptance check` and `directive` (--collect, --outcomes, --against); conjunctive DONE and 'completely built' with listed-line accounting; asks retired, never deleted; founder and external blockers on test-reachable tiers cite records; principles guarded by their own evidence; a separate read-only workflow collects every cited node, ratchets the pin against the PR base and runs the 85-mutant gate.

residual_risks.risk: The reading itself (paraphrases, required tiers, blocker classes, set-aside lines) is wrong in places
residual_risks.mitigation: Every judgement is a visible, pinned, separately reviewable edit; the founder can withdraw an ask by intent record
residual_risks.review_trigger: The founder's ruling on the reading or a reviewer's finding against a specific ask

residual_risks.risk: The static count is quoted as attained progress
residual_risks.mitigation: Labels in the summary line and README; the PR states the run counts beside it
residual_risks.review_trigger: A report citing '77/272' without its label

residual_risks.risk: The map is not re-read after a merge that changes evidence (#209 at 638457a4 is the current case)
residual_risks.mitigation: The static check and collection hold on a tree merged with 638457a4; the integrator re-reads the map at intake

dissent.handling: Recorded with thresholds; neither blocks the draft. Both bound how the verdict may be quoted.

entries.position: Count an ask met only from a CI run of its cited nodes, not from the static ceiling, before the map's counts are quoted as progress.
entries.rationale: Six statically met asks have skipped on every host checked, and the nine that cite mission requirements were not re-run; a ceiling is not an attainment.
entries.evidence_threshold: A CI run in which a statically met ask's nodes fail or skip, or any report quoting the static met count as attained
entries.review_trigger: The first CI job that runs the cited nodes and publishes `directive --outcomes`

entries.position: The label 'prompt completely built' should say it covers sections 1-77, or the preamble should be mapped, before the verdict is reported to the founder as covering the whole prompt.
entries.rationale: The 4,026-character preamble holds the 'Build this:' paragraph, the directive's headline build ask; review MWB-11 found terms there that no numbered section carries.
entries.evidence_threshold: A preamble ask that no section's ask answers, or the founder stating the preamble is part of the criterion
entries.review_trigger: The next map revision, or the founder's ruling on the reading

authority_impact.approver: Alfonso Lopez (adoption, any merge, ratifying the reading and any withdrawal of an ask); #196 integrator for intake

migration_plan: None required. The change adds data files, a checker, tests, a workflow and records; five files are added to foundry/owned-source.json. Nothing in GREG's runtime reads them. After each unit lands in #196, its tests are cited in the map and its asks recomputed, as c49572d7 did for WU-01 and WU-14.

`python -m acceptance check` then prints only its earlier line; no runtime state, ledger or grant changes

kill_criteria: `check` passes a map in which a pinned ask is missing, or a section is DONE with an open ask or an unanswered listed line
'Prompt completely built' reads yes while any ask is BUILDABLE_NOT_BUILT, an unguarded principle or open with no blocker
A mutant of a listed safeguard survives the gate on a merged head
The founder rejects the reading and the map cannot express his reading without weakening a check
decision_owner: Alfonso Lopez decides adoption, any merge, and whether to ratify the reading (required tiers, blocker classes, withdrawals); the #196 integrator decides intake and where the gates run in CI; session_01Kucyfm6YBHMTjaiC1M9hqD owns the reversible draft. The five role positions are recorded by the implementing session; the adversarial reviews were done by separate agents of this same session, not by independent sessions or humans. All five roles recommend RETAIN; two dissents are recorded.
review_trigger: Intake into #196 (re-read the map against #209 and later adoptions); the first CI run of directive-completion.yml; a CI job publishing `directive --outcomes`; the founder's ruling on the reading; or the unanswered-line count reaching 0
